text: When you design a REST API, clear structure matters. Start by choosing simple, meaningful endpoints, such as /users or /orders, and use the correct HTTP methods for each action. Always return proper status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is missing, so clients understand what happened. Good documentation helps other developers use your API without confusion. Finally, plan for versioning from the beginning, for example /v1/users, because your API will change over time. These practices make your API easier to use, maintain, and improve.
